newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Reform bust would be no disaster for Brazil - Franco.
newsitem.headline: Reform bust would be no disaster for Brazil - Franco.

text.p: Brazil's economy will not be undermined if key structural reforms failed to pass Congress before next year's elections, Central Bank international affairs director Gustavo Franco said.
"We're not on the brink of disaster," Franco told O Globo newspaper in an interview published Sunday.

"We can still improve the fiscal situation as we have been doing. Conditions for doing that could deteriorate in the medium term without civil service and pension reforms, but the situation is under control," Franco said.
"I think the real (currency) still has a lot of puff," he told the newspaper.

Government lawmakers have recently begun to concede they may not get the reforms through Congress as the 1998 presidential, congressional and state governorship elections start to dominate the political scene.

Sent to Congress two years ago, the bills are considered essential to the government's attempts to cut public spending and consolidate its anti-inflation plan. But both have run into entrenched resistance from lawmakers.
Franco told O Globo low growth would be the main consequence of failure to approve the reforms until the next Congress sits in 1999.
"Brazil's doing alright with three percent growth a year right now. Without reforms, we can't grow any faster," he said.
